prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1008; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just leave my name out of it for now, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine for this exercise. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving on a main road in Pasadena, Texas, heading toward the shopping center. Traffic had slowed down because of a light ahead.

Q: What happened next?

A: I came to a stop behind a car at the light. Then I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped forward and then back against the headrest.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: Not really. I was looking at the light and the car in front of me. I saw the bumper in my mirror a second before it hit.

Q: Did you get out of your car at the scene?

A: I got out, but I was stiff and sore right away. I had trouble turning my head to the left, and my lower back was aching.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic later that afternoon. They diagnosed a neck strain and a lower back strain and gave me muscle relaxers and a referral for physical therapy.

Q: Are you still having symptoms?

A: Yes. Sitting for long periods makes my back worse, and I've been waking up with neck stiffness. I've missed a few days of work because of it.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I'm trying to follow the treatment plan, and I'd like to be kept updated on the claim.

Q: Understood. This concludes the recorded statement. Thank you.
